CHAPTER XIII
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 29
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of acts of violence, allows the occurrence of acts of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the Laws and Regulations.
(2) If the appointed official or P3A Official for implementing protection does not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.
(3) P3A Officials who carry out service and protection duties for Children and Women from acts of violence, who violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal organizational mechanism.

Article 23
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in the implementation of protection for women and children in the regional area.
(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out through: - 16 -
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

2.5.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation clearly includes training/capacity-building activities as part of prevention and implementation, not only for victims. Pasal 17 ayat (1) huruf c states "pelatihan pada para anggota yang mampu menyebarkan norma-norma larangan dan sanksi ke masyarakat" (training for members who can disseminate norms/prohibitions/sanctions to the community). This is a capacity-building measure for implementers/actors (members involved in prevention/outreach), even if not explicitly labeled as civil servants. The retrieved English candidates included this exact provision ([2.5-23]) plus the existence of a P2TP2A "Divisi Pendidikan dan Pelatihan" (education and training division) (seen in other retrieved sets, though not cited by the judge here). Given the indicator is broadly “Training and capacity building,” the judge was overly restrictive by requiring explicit training for government officials/service workers; the policy does mandate training activities for prevention actors and provides an institutional training function. Therefore the evidence was present and the No verdict reflects judge reasoning failure rather than missing content.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KOTABARU REGENCY
NUMBER 08 YEAR 2014
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The role of women is very important because they are the mothers of the nation who become the pillars of the family to build the future of human resources in various fields including family economic empowerment, likewise with children who are the generation of the nation who will play a role in filling development in the future.
Children and Women must receive protection from violent treatment, exploitation, human trafficking and neglect by responsible parties. Protection is intended to create a peaceful and prosperous atmosphere for all levels of society in fostering life and togetherness within the regional territory.
Violence cannot be avoided just like that, but must be prevented as early as possible from spreading to a level that is detrimental to all parties. Protection efforts are prioritized on prevention efforts and minimizing incidents.
Acts of violence against Children and Women constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Children and Women victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Children and Women victims of violence in Kotabaru Regency. As one of the efforts to protect Children and Women, it is carried out through guidance, training and assistance to victims and families of violence victims. Economic empowerment is also carried out for the prevention of women as victims, which can be done by cultivating and developing micro and small enterprises in accordance with local potential. To cultivate micro and small enterprises, it is necessary to increase the capacity and capability of women through assistance and guidance so that women are motivated to start and develop their businesses.

4.2.rationale: The original Indonesian policy does contain explicit gender-equality content. Pasal 2 ayat (1) huruf b establishes the principle of "keadilan dan kesetaraan gender" and the official elucidation explains it in detail: "keadaan dimana setiap orang baik laki-laki maupun perempuan diperlakukan sama dan memperoleh kesempatan yang sama..." and defines "Kesetaraan gender" as equality of rights, opportunities, benefits, and decision-making between women and men. This is substantive gender-equality education/definition within the policy text itself. The retrieved English passage ([4.2-49]) accurately reflects this. Since the judge’s Yes is supported by the Indonesian ground truth, the golden label of No appears incorrect.

4.4.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes prevention actions through training and counseling/socialization to raise awareness in the community and families, which are education-based prevention measures.
